지키다 (to keep/observe) → stem 지키 + 어야 해요 → 지켜야 해요 (contracted). 시간을 지키다 = to be on time / keep time.

cards.english: I have to prepare a presentation.
cards.grammarNote: 준비하다 (to prepare) → 준비해야 해요. 발표 = presentation/announcement.

cards.english: I must focus on my hobby.
cards.grammarNote: 집중하다 (to focus/concentrate) → 집중해야 해요. 취미 = hobby.

cards.english: I have to finish it by Friday.
cards.grammarNote: 끝내다 (to finish) → stem 끝내 + 어야 해요 → 끝내야 해요. 까지 = by/until. 금요일 = Friday.

cards.english: You have to keep practicing to improve.
cards.grammarNote: 키우다 (to grow/develop) + 려면 = if you want to... 계속 = continuously. A motivational sentence combining -려면 and -해야 해요.

packs.name: 할 수 있어요 — Can / Able To

cards.grammarNote: 하다 (do) → stem 하 → vowel ending → add ㄹ → 할. 할 수 있어요 = can do. The base pattern for all 하다 verbs.
Replace 있어요 with 없어요 to negate: 할 수 없어요 = cannot do. 수 없어요 = there is no way.
가다 → stem 가 → vowel → add ㄹ → 갈. 갈 수 있어요 = can go.
갈 수 없어요 = cannot go. Same stem as 갈 수 있어요, just 없어요 instead.
먹다 → stem 먹 → ends in consonant ㄱ → add 을 → 먹을. 먹을 수 있어요 = can eat.
말하다 → 하 → vowel → add ㄹ → 말할. 한국어를 = Korean (object). 말할 수 있어요 = can speak.
오다 → stem 오 → vowel → add ㄹ → 올. 내일 = tomorrow. Rising intonation makes it a question.
올 수 없어요 = cannot come. 죄송해요 = I'm sorry (formal).
마시다 → stem 마시 → vowel 이 → add ㄹ → 마실. 마실 수 있어요 = can drink.
보다 → stem 보 → vowel → add ㄹ → 볼. 볼 수 있어요 = can see.
도와드리다 (honorific help) → 드리 + ㄹ = 드릴. 도와드릴 수 있어요 = can help (you, respectfully).
수영하다 → 할. 여기서 = here (에서 contracted). 수영할 수 있어요? = Can you swim?
못 (mot) is the short-form 'cannot.' 못 + verb = informal inability. Compare: 먹을 수 없어요 (more formal/deliberate).
읽다 → stem 읽 → consonant ending → add 을 → 읽을. 읽을 수 있어요 = can read.
이해하다 (to understand) → 하 → add ㄹ → 이해할. 이해할 수 있어요 = can understand.

cards.english: I can't speak Korean well yet.
cards.grammarNote: 못 (short form) + 해요 = can't do. 아직 = yet. 잘 못 해요 = can't do it well. Natural, casual phrasing.

packs.name: -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같아요 — It Seems / I Think

cards.grammarNote: Adjective + -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 = it seems / looks like. 피곤하다 → 피곤한 것 같아요. 것 = thing/fact; 같아요 = seems like.
행복하다 (to be happy) → 행복한 것 같아요. Context (she) is inferred. Korean often omits the subject when clear.
화가 나다 (anger rises) → past modifier 난 (나 + ㄴ). 화가 난 것 같아요 = seems like anger has risen = seems angry.
Action verb + -는 것 같아요 (present). 무서워하다 (to feel scared) → 무서워하는 것 같아요. For adjectives use -(으)ㄴ; for action verbs use -는.
슬프다 (to be sad) → 슬픈 (슬프 + ㄴ → 슬픈). Adjective modifier form before 것 같아요.

cards.english: It looks like they're enjoying it.
cards.grammarNote: 즐기다 (to enjoy) → action verb, present tense modifier: 즐기는. 즐기는 것 같아요 = looks like (they're) enjoying it.
걱정하다 (to worry) → 걱정하는 것 같아요. Action verb → -는 것 같아요.
지루하다 (to be bored/boring) → 지루한 것 같아요. Adjective → -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요.

cards.english: It seems like he fell in love.
cards.grammarNote: 빠지다 (to fall into) → past modifier: 빠진 (빠지 + ㄴ). 사랑에 빠지다 = to fall in love. Past tense modifier used for completed states.
불편하다 (to be uncomfortable) → 불편한 것 같아요. 불편 = discomfort. Adjective form.
울다 (to cry) + 고 있다 (progressive) → 울고 있는 것 같아요. 있는 is the modifier form of 있다. Use progressive for ongoing actions.
나아지다 (to get better) → past modifier: 나아진 (나아지 + ㄴ). 기분 = mood/feeling. Combines past action modifier with 것 같아요.
V/A stem + 지만 = but / however. 피곤하다 (to be tired) → 피곤하지만. Works with any verb or adjective. The subject is the same in both clauses.
어렵다 (to be difficult) → 어렵지만 (no stem change needed). 재미있다 = to be fun/interesting. Common pattern for expressing mixed feelings.
무섭다 (to be scary/scared) → 무섭지만. 설레다 = to be excited/flutter with anticipation. Great emotional contrast.

cards.english: I like him but we can't date.
cards.grammarNote: 좋아하다 (to like) → 좋아하지만. 사귀다 = to date. 사귈 수 없어요 = cannot date.
슬프다 (to be sad) → 슬프지만. 괜찮다 = to be okay/fine. A common phrase for expressing resilience.
화가 나다 (to be angry/anger rises) → 화가 나지만. 이해하다 = to understand.

cards.english: I miss him but I've moved on.
cards.grammarNote: 그리워하다 (to miss someone) → 그리워하지만. 이제 = now. Expression of emotional progress.

cards.english: I'm lonely but I feel free.
cards.grammarNote: 외롭다 (to be lonely) → 외롭지만 (ㅂ irregular doesn't apply with 지만; stem stays as is before consonants). 자유롭다 = to be free.

cards.english: I'm nervous but I can do it.
cards.grammarNote: 긴장되다 (to feel nervous) → 긴장되지만. 할 수 있어요 = can do it. An encouraging contrast.

cards.english: The job is boring but the pay is good.
cards.grammarNote: 지루하다 (to be boring) → 지루하지만. 월급 = monthly salary/pay. -지만 can also contrast subjects across clauses.

cards.english: I'm jealous but I'm happy for you.
cards.grammarNote: 부럽다 (to be envious/jealous) → 부럽지만. 잘됐다 = to have turned out well / good for you. A gracious emotional response.

packs.name: -(으)면 좋겠어요 / -는 게 좋아요 — I'd Better / It's Better To

cards.grammarNote: V-는 게 좋아요 = it's better to / you should [verb]. 쉬다 (to rest) → 쉬는 게 좋아요. Use this pattern to give gentle advice.
V-아야/어야 해요 = must / have to. 먹다 (to eat/take) has stem 먹 (ends in consonant) + 어야 해요 → 먹어야 해요.
가다 (to go) → 가는 게 좋아요. 병원 = hospital/clinic. This is softer than a direct command.
자다 (to sleep) → 자는 게 좋아요. 일찍 = early.
마시다 (to drink) → stem 마시 + 어야 해요 → 마셔야 해요 (contracted). 물 = water.
운동하다 (to exercise) → 운동하는 게 좋아요. 규칙적으로 = regularly.

cards.english: I have to go to the hospital.
cards.grammarNote: 가다 (to go) → 가야 해요. The stem 가 ends in vowel ㅏ → use 아야 해요 → 가 + 아야 해요 = 가야 해요.
To negate V-는 게 좋아요, use V-지 않는 게 좋아요. 무리하다 = to overwork / push too hard.
쉬다 (to rest) → stem 쉬 + 어야 해요 → 쉬어야 해요. 오늘은 = today (topic).
먹다 (to eat) → 먹는 게 좋아요. 잘 = well.
받다 (to receive) → 받는 게 좋아요. 검사를 받다 = to receive/get an examination.

cards.english: You have to take the prescribed medicine.
cards.grammarNote: 처방받다 = to be prescribed. 처방받은 약 = prescribed medicine. 먹어야 해요 = must take.

cards.english: I'm sick so I can't come.
cards.grammarNote: 아프다 (to be sick) → stem 아프 → 아파서. When the stem ends in 으 before 아/어, the 으 drops: 아프 + 아서 → 아파서. Result: I'm sick, so I can't come.

cards.english: My head hurts so I need medicine.
cards.grammarNote: 아파서 links cause (head hurts) to result (need medicine). -아서/어서 cannot be used with past tense endings — the tense is shown in the final verb.

cards.english: I'm tired so I want to sleep.
cards.grammarNote: 피곤하다 (to be tired) → 피곤해서 (하다 verbs: 하 + 여서 → 해서). 자고 싶어요 = want to sleep.

cards.english: I had a fever so I stayed home.
cards.grammarNote: 나다 (to come out/occur) → stem 나 + 아서 → 나서. 열이 나다 = to have a fever. Note: tense marker (-었어요) only on the final verb.

cards.english: It was cold so I wore a jacket.
cards.grammarNote: 춥다 (to be cold) is irregular: 춥 → 추워서 (ㅂ irregular: ㅂ → 워 before vowels).

cards.english: My stomach hurts so I can't eat.
cards.grammarNote: 배가 아프다 = stomach hurts. 아파서 = because it hurts. 못 먹어요 = can't eat.

cards.english: I feel better so I'm going out.
cards.grammarNote: 나아지다 (to get better/improve) → 나아져서. 나가다 = to go out.

cards.english: I was dizzy so I sat down.
cards.grammarNote: 어지럽다 (to be dizzy) → ㅂ irregular: 어지러워서. 앉다 = to sit → 앉았어요 (past).

cards.english: My throat is sore so I'm drinking water.
cards.grammarNote: 목이 아프다 = throat hurts. 아파서 = because it hurts. Direct cause-and-result chain.

cards.english: My arm is broken so I can't write.
cards.grammarNote: 골절되다 (to be fractured) → 골절돼서 (되 + 어서 → 돼서). 쓸 수 없어요 = cannot write.

cards.english: I rested so I feel better.
cards.grammarNote: 쉬다 (to rest) → stem 쉬 + 어서 → 쉬어서. 나아지다 = to improve/get better. 몸 = body.

cards.english: I keep sneezing so I think I have a cold.
cards.word: 계속 재채기가 나서 감기인 것 같아요.
cards.romanized: Gyesok jaechaegiga naseo gamgiin geot gatayo.
cards.grammarNote: 계속 재채기가 나다 = to keep sneezing. 나서 = because [it] comes out. 감기 = cold. 인 것 같아요 = seems to be.

packs.name: 내 vs 제 — My (Informal vs Formal)

cards.grammarNote: 나 = I in informal/casual speech. Used with close friends, younger people, or in casual writing. 내 (my) comes from 나 + 의.
저 = I in formal/polite speech. Used with strangers, elders, superiors, or anyone you should show respect to. 제 (my) comes from 저 + 의.
내 = my (informal). 나 + 의 → 내 (contracted). Use with close friends and family in casual speech.
제 = my (formal). 저 + 의 → 제 (contracted). Use with anyone you address politely — teachers, strangers, elders, colleagues.
이야 is the informal copula (to be). Use with close friends: 이게 내 책이야 (casual) vs 이게 제 책이에요 (polite).

cards.english: Which form to use with a teacher?
cards.grammarNote: Always use 저/제 with teachers, bosses, strangers, and anyone older. Use 나/내 with close friends, younger siblings, or in casual text messages.
아프다 = to hurt / to be sick. Pattern: [body part] + 이/가 + 아파요. The subject marker 이/가 marks the body part that hurts.
머리 (head) ends in 이 (vowel) → 가 is used. 머리가 아파요.
배 (stomach/belly) ends in vowel → 가. 배가 아파요.
목 (throat/neck) ends in consonant ㄱ → 이. 목이 아파요.
등 (back) ends in consonant ㅇ → 이. 등이 아파요.
어디 (where) + 가 (subject marker) + 아파요? This is the standard way to ask where someone is in pain.
몸 (body) + 이 + 아파요. This can mean either 'I feel sick' or 'my body aches all over.'
온몸 = whole body. 온몸이 아파요 = my whole body hurts.
너무 = too much / very (in spoken Korean, 너무 often just means 'very'). 너무 아파요 = it hurts a lot.
